page.layout: Running head top centre and page number top left. Two woodcut medallion portraits centred at the top, with their legends around them (left: EVDOCIA; right: DIOGENES ROMANVS). Below them, one column of running text in two paragraphs. No margin notes, no notes under the text.

main_text.p: EVDOCIA cum filiis imperat Constantinopoli post Constantinum Ducam,anno mundi 5031. à Christo nato 1069. Poterat muliebri fortasse prudentia hęc,si foris cessassent bella, imperiũ domi administrare: sed lacessentibus undique imperium barbaris,vicit eorum sententia,qui rebus præficiendũ virum appositum ac idoneum contendebāt. Quare iurisiurandi oblita,quo marito Ducæ,morieti, se obstrinxerat, non superinducturam se virum, etiam si coacta esset, Romanū cognomine Diogenem,post menses imperij septem,in virum Eudocia assumit, qui republ. prudentia ac fortitudine tueretur: at pœnituit statim Eudociam,quòd vir hic insolens rem ad se totam traheret. Vide Egna. lib.2.Cosmog. Mun.lib.4.

ROMANVS Diogenes Eudociæ vir,imperat Constantinopoli, anno mundi 5032. à Christo nato 1070. duas hic suscepit expeditiones vario rerum successu : prior quidē optimè cessit,posteriorautem pessimè:nam vel fugatis vel cæsis militibus suis ipse Imperator Constantinopolitanus capitur:quod ad eam diem nunquã contigerat. Ferunt tamen Turcam nomine Azan,ad primũ huius euentus nuncium, vix credentem constitisse:mox ad se adductum Ro.Diogenem, & cognitū, in precio habuisse: ac amplis donatum muneribus, pace inita, dimisisse. Sed ad primum aduersæ cladis nuncium, ut ferè fit, omnia Constantinopoli iam mutata erat:Eudocia nempe relegata est:Romano abdicatum est imperium : Michaël Imperator creatus, Romanum Diogenē victum, deditúmque , contra iusiurandũ exoculat, ac in insulam deportat, ubi ab uxore Eudocia sepelitur, post annos imperij ferè quotuor. Vide ut supra.

page.notes: Printed "morieti" read as shown; uncertain of the vowel. "quotuor" is as printed (apparent printing error for quatuor). Figures 5031, 5032, 1069, 1070 are in old-style form and read as shown. Medallion legends are printed on the woodcuts and are given as lines above the text.
